h1: 10 best Gong alternatives.Compare prices, call recording and coaching.
intro: Choose a tool for meeting notes, call coaching or managing sales opportunities. Compare each Gong competitor’s price, useful features and extra charges.

providers.name: Avoma vs Gong
providers.fit: Structured coaching with published add-on prices
providers.price: Startup records the calls. Conversation Intelligence adds scoring and coaching; Revenue Intelligence adds forecasting.
providers.good: Custom scorecards, automated call reviews and coaching suggestions give managers a clear review process. Free viewers can watch and comment. Paid add-ons can be assigned to the people who need them.
providers.weak: The $19 annual-billing headline buys the base recorder. A recorder with coaching costs $48; adding Revenue Intelligence brings it to $77. Bulk historical imports can also carry a fee.
providers.verdict: Worth paying for when managers use scorecards and review calls every week. Buy only the add-ons those people need.

providers.name: Fathom vs Gong
providers.fit: Discovery calls, demos and meeting reviews
providers.price: Business adds AI scorecards, CRM field sync and a shared view of meetings on a deal.
providers.good: The free plan records and transcribes meetings. Business adds team review tools, with recordings and notes grouped by deal.
providers.weak: Business requires two paid users. Its supported-platform guide excludes ordinary phone calls, including Zoom Phone.
providers.verdict: A good choice for coaching demos and discovery meetings. Cold calling teams need a recorder that supports their dialer.

providers.name: Fireflies vs Gong
providers.fit: Meeting records, analytics and flexible sales workflows
providers.price: Business includes conversation analytics; advanced AI actions have a separate credit bill.
providers.good: It brings meetings, supported dialer calls and uploaded recordings into one searchable library. Sales tools add scorecards, CRM updates and deal insights.
providers.weak: The 30 included AI credits are a one-time allowance. Extra credit packs start at $5/month for 50 credits. Automatic subscriptions and upgrades can increase the bill; check those settings before enabling AI workflows.
providers.verdict: Good value for call review. Budget for the AI tasks you enable and keep automatic credit upgrades under control.

providers.name: tl;dv vs Gong
providers.fit: Coaching, playbook checks and reports across meetings
providers.price: Business includes the coaching tools and unlimited multi-meeting AI questions, without usage-based AI fees.
providers.good: Managers can find patterns across meetings, check how closely reps follow a sales playbook and schedule reports.
providers.weak: Pro limits multi-meeting questions and leaves out the full coaching package. Business still has recording limits, including a three-hour meeting cap.
providers.verdict: Shortlist Business for weekly coaching and reports across meetings. If you only need notes, start with a lower tier.

providers.name: Sybill vs Gong
providers.price: Pro covers notes and follow-up. Business adds CRM context, deal workspaces and Autofill for ten CRM fields.
providers.good: Meeting summaries and follow-up drafts reduce the admin after a call. Ask Sybill lets managers review sales conversations and deal details.
providers.weak: Business costs three times the Pro subscription. AI tasks have weekly credit allowances, and extra packs cost $100 for 5,000 credits. Basic recording and summaries continue when AI credits run out.
providers.verdict: Start with Pro if the main problem is admin. Pay for Business only when the CRM automation saves enough work to justify the jump.

providers.name: Jiminny vs Gong
providers.fit: Managers running a regular coaching programme
providers.price: Custom quote, a 12-month minimum and a one-time setup fee. No platform fee or usage credits.
providers.good: Call libraries, scorecards and team insights support organised coaching. Deal-risk views help managers connect the conversation to the opportunity. Separate seat types cover recorders, managers and listeners.
providers.weak: Dollar rates and the setup fee are missing from its current pricing page. Monthly billing still carries a year-long commitment.
providers.verdict: Consider it for a team with regular manager-led coaching. Get the setup fee and full annual price before the demo.

providers.name: ZoomInfo Chorus vs Gong
providers.fit: Coaching connected to account and deal context
providers.price: Chorus requires a quote. ZoomInfo's public pricing does not supply a Chorus dollar total.
providers.good: Scorecards, coaching initiatives and smart playlists help managers review calls. Deal-risk signals and account context can support opportunity reviews.
providers.weak: The public pages leave the subscription cost and minimum purchase unanswered. Get Chorus seats, data access and required integrations itemised in the same offer.
providers.verdict: Shortlist it for coaching that uses ZoomInfo’s account context. Demand an itemised quote before deciding it offers better value than Gong.

providers.name: Salesloft vs Gong
providers.fit: Teams that want coaching inside their outreach workflow
providers.price: For new integrated setups, price Salesloft, Clari Copilot and the Conversation Intelligence integration together.
providers.good: Call summaries, scorecards and live prompts keep coaching close to a rep’s follow-up work.
providers.weak: There is no public dollar price. New implementations from July 2026 require both subscriptions. Dialing and forecasting are listed separately as add-ons.
providers.verdict: Compare the package if your team already works in Salesloft. Buying both subscriptions just to record meetings is poor value.

providers.name: Outreach Kaia vs Gong
providers.fit: Live assistance and connected sales follow-up
providers.price: Amplify Essentials covers conversation intelligence. Plus adds sequencing; Pro adds forecasting. All require a quote.
providers.good: Live prompts can surface useful information during a meeting. Managers get recordings and automated scores to review afterwards.
providers.weak: AI usage, selected connectors and implementation can add to the seat bill. Public package descriptions do not give a dollar total.
providers.verdict: Useful when reps need live guidance and connected follow-up. Ask sales for the expected AI bill as well as seat prices.

providers.name: Dialpad Sell vs Gong
providers.fit: Calling and coaching in the same system
providers.price: Annual rates: Essentials $39, Advanced $59 and Premium $79 per user/month. Premium includes AI scorecards and Coaching Hub.
providers.good: Recording, transcripts and CRM logging sit alongside the phone system. Advanced adds live guidance; Premium brings scorecards and playbooks into the calling workflow.
providers.weak: Local-dialing number packages and selected extras cost more. Replacing a working phone system also creates migration work.
providers.verdict: Strong value when the team needs both calling and structured reviews. If the phone setup already works, compare the cost and effort of adding coaching to it first.

resourceIntro: Copy these into a vendor email or keep them beside your renewal quote. No signup required.
resource:
1. What is the full first-year cost for our recording users and managers, including platform fees, setup, AI usage and required add-ons?
2. Can you capture calls from our exact dialer and meeting tools, and save the right notes and fields in our CRM?
3. Show us how a manager reviews a real call, scores it and gives the rep a useful next step. Which plan includes that?
4. Can we export our recordings, transcripts and coaching records? What will transfer from our current tool, and what costs extra?
5. What is the minimum term, when can we reduce seats, and what price and notice period apply at renewal?
resourceAside: Get the answers in the quote.
resourceNote: Use the same questions for every shortlisted vendor. A written price and a working example make the decision much easier.

faqs.q: What is the best Gong alternative?
faqs.a: Fathom suits meeting capture and demo reviews. Fireflies adds flexible sales tools. Compare Avoma and tl;dv for regular coaching, or Dialpad Sell if you also need a phone system. For forecasting, compare the specific management features your team needs.

Gong publishes its pricing structure, but no dollar rate. It charges per-user licences plus a platform fee. Additional applications and selected AI usage can affect the total. Ask for an itemised quote for the seats and features your team needs.

faqs.q: Is there a free Gong alternative?
faqs.a: Fathom's free plan is a practical starting point for recording and transcribing meetings. Fireflies also has a free plan, with 400 minutes of team storage and limited AI summaries. Free meeting tools cover a narrower job than a paid coaching and forecasting platform.
Avoma Startup plus Conversation Intelligence costs $48 per recorder/month on annual billing when that person has both licences. Compare that setup with your Gong quote to decide which costs less.

faqs.q: Can Fathom replace Gong for cold call coaching?
faqs.a: Use Fathom for demos and discovery meetings. Its support guide excludes ordinary phone calls, including Zoom Phone. For coaching dialer calls, choose a compatible recorder.
Neither publishes enough pricing to settle that. Compare quotes for the same number of reps and managers, required features, setup and contract term.

Avoma offers a separate Revenue Intelligence add-on with forecasting. Outreach places forecasting in Amplify Pro, and Salesloft lists it as an add-on. Check the exact forecasting task: deal summaries, manager forecasts and consolidated revenue projections are different capabilities.

faqs.q: Can CallTeam coach our salespeople or run the calls?
faqs.a: Yes. CallTeam can review calls, improve scripts and practise openings, objections and qualification with your team. We can also prepare and run a cold calling campaign, follow up with buyers and book qualified meetings.
